summary: Forest Service fire tower on South Mountain in Ripton, built 1941 and destroyed by wind by January 1951; no source describes the summit today.

facts.design: 41-foot prefabricated timber tower with a 14-foot-square glassed-in platform (1941 newspaper); a 1943 survey describes it as wood, about 50 feet high
facts.status_note: Wind destroyed the tower by January 1951; no source describes the summit or any remains today.

notes_for_editor: Height conflict: the April 1941 newspaper gives 41 ft (the record's 12.5 m matches this); the 1943 survey description says wood, about 50 ft. The facts give 41 ft in the design string only and height_m is left out. Name year conflict: Forest Lookouts says 1953, and the historical marker says the state named a mountain after Frost in 1955. A search summary mentioned a 1953 legislative naming that I did not open, so it is not cited. The April 1941 item says 'just completing' and the October 1941 item says 'completed ... early last spring', so the 1941 build year is an inference from these two. The NGS-style station description places the tower about 5.0 miles northeast of East Middlebury; I did not check that against the record coordinates. No source describes the summit or any remains today, and the Route 125 wayside is not the tower site. No new photos found. Confidence medium.
